The optimal cut-off for Fasting Plasma Glucose was estimated as 104 milligram\/dL with a sensitivity of 82.3% and specificity of 89.4%.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAt present recommended threshold of 6.5%, HbA1c is more specific and less sensitive in diagnosing the newly detected diabetes in undiagnosed population from community settings.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/dx.plos.org\/10.1371\/journal.pone.0242415\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/dx.plos.org\/10.1371\/journal.pone.0242415\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EQ.\u003C\/b\u003EWhat is insensible fluid loss? How does it effect of syncope.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EInsensible fluid loss is the amount of body fluid lost daily that is not easily measured, from the respiratory system, skin, and water in the excreted stool. The exact amount is unmeasurable but is estimated to be between 40 to 800mL\/day in the average adult without comorbidities. A total loss of approximately 600 to 800mL\/day characterizes 30 to 50% of all water loss, contingent on the level of water consumed. Thus insensible water loss is a significant component of water balance and needs to be routinely monitored.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Clues to hypovolemia include hydration of mucous membranes, skin turgor, resting heart rate, and intensity of peripheral pulses. Additionally, blood pressure particularly orthostatic changes and urinary output, are also important indicators of fluid status gleaned from a physical examination.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK544219\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK544219\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELEARNING LONG CASE:-A 65 yr old female with syncope"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Ch3 class=\"post-title entry-title\"\u003ECASE OF A 65 YEARS OLD FEMALE WITH SYNCOPE .\u003C\/h3\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"post-body-container\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"post-body entry-content float-container\" id=\"post-body-417747530312507381\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardians' signed informed consent. This Elog reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003EThis is the case of a 65 years old lady ,housewife resident of Chinatunalgudam.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe patient presented to the casualty after an episode of loss of consciousness .\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Patient was apparently asymptomatic six days ago , when she had an episode of loss of consciousness\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;, associated with sweating , and after walking for a long time .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENot associated with palpitation , flushing , chest pain , muscle weakness , slurring of speech, headache \u0026nbsp;.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EThe patient was brought to the casualty and given medication and recovered completely \u0026nbsp;.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E6 days ago - History of chest pain\u003Cspan class=\"Apple-converted-space\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E( sudden onset , in the centre of chest , squeezing type , non progressive , not radiating ) with shortness of breath following exertion , which were both relieved on rest .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EShe went to an RMP and was given an anti hypertensive agent .( which she consumed for the first time 3 days ago )\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENo similar complaints in the past\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EShe is a known case of hypertension since 3days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENot a known case of diabetes mellitus , asthma , tb , cerebrovascular accidents , coronary artery disease .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENo blood transfusions .\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EHistory of treatment for cellulitis of leg .\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFAMILY HISTORY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E3 siblings with DM\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EMixed diet , normal appetite\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EAdequate sleep\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENormal bowel and bladder movements\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ENo allergies\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EAddiction - sutta- 4 cigarettes\/ day since 40 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EAlcohol or toddy - 1 glass daily\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EDaily routine\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EWake up - 7 am\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E8 am - breakfast (rice )and tea\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EAfternoon (2:30pm)- lunch ( rice and curry )\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EDinner - 9pm -\u003C\/span\u003Erice and curry .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003ESleep - 10 pm\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EGENERAL cooperative\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003EModerately built and moderately nourished\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s2\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p3\"\u003E\u003Cspan my blog! I am U.AKANKSHA a 4th year medical student.This is an online\u0026nbsp;E-log Entry Blog to discuss, understand and review the clinical scenarios and data analysis of patients so as to develop my clinical competency in comprehending clinical cases, and providing evidence-based inputs.It also reflects patient centered online learning portfolio.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENote:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u0026nbsp;The\u0026nbsp;cases have been shared after taking consent from the patient\/guardian. All\u0026nbsp;names and other identifiers have been removed to secure and respect the privacy of the patient and the family.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cu\u003EConsent:\u003C\/u\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003EAn informed consent has been taken from the patient in the presence of the family attenders and other witnesses as well and the document has been conserved securely for future references.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 43 year old male was brought to the casualty with comlains of involuntary movements of body since today morning.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS\u003C\/b\u003E:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe Patient was apparently asymptomatic 4 days back when he had a binge of alcohol . he lost consciousness at his workplace and was taken to the hospital. At the hospital, the correction fluids were given and the patient was sent home. Today morning he had 2 episodes of involuntary movement of body (tonic movements with stiffening of body) lasting 1-2 minutes and relieved on itself.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHis wife checked his grbs at home after this episode and it was found to be 60mg\/dl after which he was rushed to the hospital. In the hospital the correction was done inspite of which involuntary movements continued. He was then brought to our hospital.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo uprolling of eyes or loss of consciousness during the episodes.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo c\/o vomitings, headache, frothing from mouth, deviation of mouth, tongue bite, post ictal confusion, involuntary micturition\/defecation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\"\u003E\u003Ciframe allowfullscreen=\"allowfullscreen\" class=\"b-hbp-video b-uploaded\" frameborder=\"0\" height=\"266\" id=\"BLOGGER-video-62c1a1beff8000e5-9245\" mozallowfullscreen=\"mozallowfullscreen\" src=\"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/video.g?token=AD6v5dxRyKIA9axr5Vz_XTshnSCBvtX9eV-cXYO8BjZZjzAvLaQvaxFBdYuLpwcwB7B8EEySrf_RTLinF5C_vq0lO2CI_YmHkmc_1YDhTbWUJo-DQKYfmEv5Tn5A7285lEWUca0EoiM\" webkitallowfullscreen=\"webkitallowfullscreen\" width=\"320\"\u003E\u003C\/iframe\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo similar complains in the past.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EK\/C\/O DM-II since 5 years on insulin. He was diagnosed with DM-II Incidently during an episode of fever for which he was initially prescribed OHA'S. The patient used to skip taking his medication. Due non compliance and very high sugars he was then shifted to insulin.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EN\/k\/c\/o HTN, CVA, CAD, Bronchial asthma, thyroid disorders.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDAILY ROUTINE :\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe patient works as an attender in a college.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe lives with his wife and three children.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe doesn't always follow his routine and go to the college.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe gets up in the morning and freshens up and has breakfast. After his family leaves for work\/college, he either goes to college or goes out with his friends and drinks alcohol.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe often skips meals\u0026nbsp; as he forgets about them while he is drinking alcohol. He often consumes food late at night when he is very hungry.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe alcohol consumption has increased in the last 1 year.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn enquiring about the reason of chronic alcoholism with his family, they say that they can't think of any triggers as such.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL
